samples_reviewed.question_text: What time does the clock show?
What time does the clock show?
What time does the clock show?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both verbs are served by distinct item types: reading is asked as What time does the clock show, and writing is asked by having the pupil set the clock to a stated time, with the analog face implied in both directions.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three granularities named are present - exact hours such as 5:00 and 9:00, half hours such as 7:30 and 12:30, and quarter hours in both forms, quarter past in the 2:15 and 6:15 reading items and quarter to in 5:45 and 3:45.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Two of the three reading items put an off-curriculum time among the choices - 2:10 in one option list and 9:25 in another. A Grade 1 pupil taught only hour, half hour and quarter hour has no basis for reading a minute hand at ten or twenty-five past, so those decoys test a skill the competency deliberately withholds at this level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The set alternates between recognising a displayed time from four choices and constructing a time on the clock face, and the times sampled span morning and midday hours including the 12 o'clock case.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty rises along the intended line, from whole hours to half past to the quarter positions, rather than by varying the hour number alone, and the reading items pit the answer against neighbouring hours which is the real confusion to train out.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Hours stay within the 12-hour analog face, minute values are confined to 00, 15, 30 and 45 in the keys, and no 24-hour or minute-level precision creeps in.
